reason: The cited evidence (E1, E3) supports that heat treatment improves the passive film and corrosion resistance of the Cantor alloy, but none of the passages address wear, film disruption, repassivation kinetics, or tribo-corrosion synergy. The key mechanistic premises about sliding wear and coupled degradation are therefore unsupported by the provided evidence.
premises: CoCrFeMnNi forms a robust passive oxide film that can be enhanced by heat treatment
Sliding wear mechanically disrupts this passive film, exposing fresh metal
Exposed metal corrodes faster than the film can repassivate, causing synergistic degradation
The repassivation kinetics are insufficient to restore the film between wear cycles under moderate conditions
The coupled response is governed by this film disruption–repassivation competition
